get.summary:
Deliberately not cached: the returned URL embeds the caller's origin, which GetWebAppUrl resolves from the X-Origin
header. The output cache does vary by that header (See AppResponseCachePolicy.CacheRequestAsync), but a CDN edge
does not unless it is configured to, so a shared-cached response would hand one origin's sign-in URL to a caller
coming from another, sending the resulting sign-in link to the wrong origin.

post.summary:
Changing an account identifier (user name, e-mail, phone) takes TWO proofs, and this policy is the first of them:
    1. That you still hold the current account. string AuthPolicies.ELEVATED_ACCESS is only granted
    after the user quotes back a 6-digit code that Task<ElevatedAccessTokenSentDto> UserController.SendElevatedAccessToken(CancellationToken cancellationToken) sent to the identifiers the
    account ALREADY has (its confirmed e-mail / phone). Someone holding only a stolen access token cannot produce it.
1. That you hold the new identifier. Task UserController.SendChangeEmailToken(SendEmailTokenRequestDto request, CancellationToken cancellationToken) /
    Task UserController.SendChangePhoneNumberToken(SendPhoneTokenRequestDto request, CancellationToken cancellationToken) then send a second code to the NEW address, and
    Task UserController.ChangeEmail(ChangeEmailRequestDto request, CancellationToken cancellationToken) / Task UserController.ChangePhoneNumber(ChangePhoneNumberRequestDto request, CancellationToken cancellationToken) only apply the change once it comes back.
    Without the first proof the second one is worthless: the attacker picks the new address himself, so his own inbox
    is the only thing he has to control - and afterwards every recovery path (password reset, magic-link sign-in, OTP)
    points at him. Note the policy sits on the `Send*` half, so following the e-mailed link to finish the change
    does not prompt for a second code. `ChangeUserName` has no second proof at all, which is why it needs this one.

Setting AcceptedOn to null hides the user from the tenant's users list and prevents auto signing into that tenant,
    but the user can re-join later by switching into it again, as long as the TenantMembership record exists.
    Leaving a membership that is ALREADY pending deletes it instead, which is how an invitation gets declined. There
is no other way to get rid of one: setting AcceptedOn to null again changes nothing while still reporting success,
and the tenant admin cannot remove it either, because UserManagementController.EnsureUserIsInCurrentTenant only
reaches accepted memberships. Without this, anyone holding Tenant_Manage could pin a tenant card carrying text of
their choosing into an arbitrary user's tenant list, permanently.

get.summary:
Articles 15 and 20: everything the app holds about the signed-in account, as a zip.
    Behind string AuthPolicies.ELEVATED_ACCESS, the gate Delete uses - a full copy of an identity is
worth as much to a stolen token as deleting it is. Rate limited for the reason Article 12(5) exists.

put.summary:
Enrolling a passkey adds a NEW way to sign in, so it belongs with the other account-factor changes behind elevated
access (compare Task UserController.Delete(CancellationToken cancellationToken), Task UserController.ChangeUserName(ChangeUserNameRequestDto request, CancellationToken cancellationToken) and Task UserController.RevokeSession(Guid id, CancellationToken cancellationToken)). Without this,
an access token stolen for a few minutes buys a credential that survives a password change AND revoking every
session, because nothing on those paths touches WebAuthnCredential - and the account owner has no UI that lists it.

post.summary: Turns a recording made by the AI chat panel's microphone into the text it puts in the message box.

Reads a whole assistant answer out loud, answering with audio the AI chat panel plays through Butil.
    It accepts the text itself rather than the id of a message because nothing stores the conversation -
AppChatbot holds it in memory for the lifetime of one SignalR connection - so there is no id that
would name an answer. The signature AppChatbot sent with the answer stands in for that id; without it
this endpoint reads out whatever it is sent, which is a text to speech api billed to whoever runs the app.

Starts a voice call. Audio flows browser-to-provider over WebRTC; the call itself is created here with the
server's key, prompt and tools, and VoiceCallRunner stays in it.

Takes an image the user attached to an AI chat message and answers with the id it was stored under, which is
    all the client needs to build the attachment url it puts in the message.
    The id is minted here rather than accepted from the client: an attachment id is the whole address of a blob
(See string AttachmentController.GetFilePath(Guid attachmentId, AttachmentKind kind)), so a caller-chosen one would let a user overwrite somebody else's attachment -
their profile image included - by naming its id.

AddressProbeOutcome.description: What the add flow found at an address.

serverAddress.description: Where the health report is read, `https://host`, as the app's `/.well-known/bit-app.json` names it.

hasStaticFrontEnd.description: The app's pages are hosted statically, so its server's `/health` is what a visitor's wait is timed on.

templateVersion.description: The bit template version the app says it's made with, or null when it doesn't say.

appTitle.description: The app's own name, from its web app manifest, to suggest as the project's.

isAlreadyAdded.description: Whether a project of the same address is already watched in this tenant.

signature.description: The server's signature over string? AiChatMessage.Content (See string AiChatProtocol.Signature); null on anything the assistant didn't write.

AiChatMessage.description:
One message of the conversation a voice call carries on (See List<AiChatMessage> StartVoiceCallRequestDto.ChatMessagesHistory).
The text chat sends its conversation in Bit.BlazorUI.AI's own wire format instead (See AiChatProtocol).
AiChatMessageRole AiChatMessage.Role and string? AiChatMessage.Signature aren't trusted on the way in: an assistant message is the assistant's only
where the signature checks out, and anything else is replayed to the model as the user's (See AppChatbot.AsProvablySaid).

code.description: Null when the customer's app answered with an error instead, such as `access_denied`.

iss.description: RFC 9207's issuer, which must name the app the approval was asked of.

timeZoneId.description: The IANA time zone of whoever adds the project, which its SLA months first follow.

instanceName.description: The instance that answered: the values below are read from that process, not from the deployment.

applicationVersion.description: Of the answering instance alone - a rolling deployment leaves the others on the old one.

timeZone.description: The operating system's, on the answering instance.

availableMemoryBytes.description: What the runtime may use: in a container its limit, not the host's memory.

usedMemoryBytes.description: The process's working set the moment the report was read.

uptime.description: Since the process started, which a deployment, a crash or an idle shutdown all reset.

supportedCultures.description: Empty when the server runs culture-invariant.

trustedOrigins.description: The origins CORS accepts, which is also what the forwarded host is checked against.

trustedOriginsRegex.description: Trusted on top of string[] DeploymentConfigurationDto.TrustedOrigins, so an empty list is not the whole answer.

forwardedHeadersConfigured.description: Without it X-Forwarded-* is ignored: every client ip is the proxy's, and links carry the internal host.

blazorMode.description: Null where the process renders nothing, which a standalone api does not.

backgroundJobsUseIsolatedStorage.description: In-memory Hangfire storage: jobs do not survive a restart, and no other instance sees them.

webPushConfigured.description: Web push signs its own messages, so nothing else says whether the browser channel can work.

minimumSupportedAndroidAppVersion.description: Below these, a client is told to update before it may go on (See ForceUpdate).

DeploymentConfigurationDto.description:
Effective settings of this deployment that no health check reports, never a secret: a credential is a boolean saying
whether it is set. Under scale-out one instance answers; what holds for that process alone is grouped behind
string? DeploymentConfigurationDto.InstanceName.

DraftTranslationsRequestDto.description: An AI draft of a text in the languages the team hasn't written it in yet, for them to review.

sentToOtherDevices.description: Pushed to the user's other sessions - only the ones trusted in their own right (See `UserSession.Trusted`).

ElevatedAccessTokenSentDto.description:
Which channels `UserController.SendElevatedAccessToken` reached - only the server knows which identifiers are
confirmed. Channels rather than identifiers, because the caller already holds the e-mail and the phone number.

FollowStatusPageRequestDto.description: A visitor's browser following a page by push.

today.description: Today, in the time zone the counts were asked for.

days.description: Every day with something to count, oldest first, the days Trials still running will end on included.

licenseDelays.description:
Every project licensed after its Trial, by the day it was licensed and the days since its Trial began: how many
projects each pair has.

teamsByProjects.description: Teams with a License by how many projects they licensed: one, two, three to five, six or more.

teamProjects.description: The projects those teams licensed, each team's counted once per project.

peopleInLicensedTeams.description: The people who are accepted members of a team with a License, each counted once.

GrowthDataDto.description: Everything the growth page counts, from the first day there was anything to count to the last Trial's end.

projectsMade.description: Projects bit Fabric first heard of that day: by their Trial, or by their first License when they had none.

projectsLicensed.description: Projects that got their first License that day.

teamsLicensed.description: Teams that got their first License that day.

inProduction.description: Licensed projects whose production environment monitoring started watching that day, and still watches.

trialsEndedLicensed.description: Of those, the ones whose project holds a License now.

trialsConverted.description:
Trials counted as converted on that day: the later of the Trial's end and the project's first License, so a share
taken as of any day knows only what had happened by then.

GrowthDayDto.description: One day's counts. A Trial bit CLI asked for from CI counts in none of them.

GrowthLicenseDelayDto.description: How many projects got their first License on DateOnly GrowthLicenseDelayDto.Day, int GrowthLicenseDelayDto.Days days after their Trial began.

HealthCheckStatus.description: Mirrors Microsoft.Extensions.Diagnostics.HealthChecks.HealthStatus, which the client doesn't reference.

returnUrl.description: URL for redirection after user confirmation, used when sending a confirmation email to an unconfirmed user.

holder.description: Whom the license names: the team that holds it, by its title. Never a person, since the license goes into git.

projectId.description: The team's project the license is for, whose page shows it.

IssuedLicenseDto.description: A free license the license page issued, with what it says, for the page to show.

code.description:
The one-time code bit CLI made for the link and waits with: it reads the license once with it (See
ILicenseController.Claim). Empty when there is no bit CLI waiting.

teamId.description: The team that holds the license, one the signed-in account is a member of (See ILicenseController.GetTeams).

IssueLicenseRequestDto.description: What the license page sends for a project's free license, from the link bit CLI printed.

projectId.description: The team's project it is for.

bitProjectId.description: The project's id in its bit.json, which the license names.

issuedBy.description: Who got it; null once their account is gone.

license.description: The license itself, for the prompt the page copies again.

LicenseDto.description: A license a team holds, as the Licenses page lists it.

LicenseResponseDto.description: A license as bit CLI writes it into bit.json; null when there is none to give.

title.description: The team's title, or its name when it has none: what the license names as its holder.

LicenseTeamDto.description: A team the signed-in account may get a license for: an active one it accepted, the one it accepted first first.

checkedAt.description: When the newest report was read.

reportMs.description: How long reading the newest report took.

homePageMs.description: How long the home page took in the round that read the newest report, from bit Fabric's own server.

homePageVisitorMs.description: How long a visitor waited for it in that round, through the cache in front of the app; null when no cache answered.

applicationVersion.description: The build the app runs, from its report (the commit after a '+').

lastRestartedAt.description: When the same build last started again on a new instance (See ProjectStartDto.IsDeploy).

regions.description: The regions whose last round counts, such as "Germany".

networkReadings.description: The newest reading of each of the bitplatform Network's locations, with the data center it ran in.

MonitoringDetailsDto.description: A project's page: the project and its last report, entry by entry.

name.description: What alerts and status pages call it: the project's name, with the environment after it unless that is Production.

projectId.description: The project it is an environment of.

environment.description: Production, Test, Staging or a name the team gave.

serverAddress.description: Null when the report is read on the address itself.

iconId.description: The app's own icon, served as an attachment (`api/v1/Attachment/GetAttachment/{IconId}/ProjectIcon`); null for none.

connectionProblem.description: Why the connection was lost, for one that needs reconnecting, in the reader's language (See ProjectConnectionProblems).

uptime30Days.description: The share of the last 30 days the app worked, of the time it was watched; null before the first round.

medianMs.description: The median time the home page took over the last 24 hours, in milliseconds, past any cache: the server's own.

medianVisitorMs.description:
The median time a visitor waited for the home page over the last 24 hours, through the cache in front of the app;
null when no cache answered it, which leaves one number, int? MonitoringDto.MedianMs.

responseLast24Hours.description: The last 24 hours' hourly medians, oldest first, 0 for an hour without a round.

last30Days.description:
The last 30 days in the time zone the cards were asked for, oldest first, today last, each colored by how its rounds
went (bitfabric-internal/specs/monitoring.md, The projects page): the card's day bars.

failingChecks.description: The checks failing or slow right now, by what the app calls them.

ongoingIncidentId.description: The open incident, when one is open, which "I'm on it" and the team's updates name.

ongoingIncident.description: The open incident's title in the reader's language, when one is open.

hasCacheWarning.description: Whether the last answer came from a cache that ignored the query string (bitfabric-internal/specs/monitoring.md, Response time).

locations.description: The bitplatform Network's locations the project is checked from besides Germany, by code (See NetworkLocations).

scans.description: The newest scan of each kind bit Fabric runs, as the card's scans row shows it (bitfabric-internal/specs/scanners.md).

MonitoringDto.description: One environment of a project as its card shows it, and as the top of its page does.

projectId.description: The environment's id, under the name the Network's code writes (src/Network).

responseMs.description: How long the answer took, redirects within the app included; null when it didn't answer.

error.description: Why it didn't answer, in a few words, such as `timeout`.

cacheHit.description: The answer carried an `Age`, `cf-cache-status: HIT` or `X-Cache: HIT` header.

location.description: The location's code, such as `enam` (See NetworkLocations).

colo.description: The data center the readings ran in, such as `IAD`, from Cloudflare's `/cdn-cgi/trace`.

NetworkResultsDto.description: What one location of the bitplatform Network found, posted back after each batch of its minute's targets.

accepted.description: How many of the results were stored; one for a project the location doesn't time is ignored.

projectId.description: The environment's id, under the name the Network's code reads (src/Network), which deploys on its own.

url.description:
The https address to time: the home page, which the Network asks for with a query string of its own (a new GUID each
time), or a static front end's server's `/health` (See IsServerHealth).

isServerHealth.description: The app's front end is hosted statically, so its server's `/health` is timed instead, as is, with no cache check.

NetworkTargetDto.description: A project one location of the bitplatform Network times every minute.

redirectUrl.description:
Built server-side from the redirect uri already validated against the client's registration, so the page can
navigate to it without validating anything itself.

OAuthApprovalDto.description: The one url the browser should now leave for.

clientId.description: An https url to a Client ID Metadata Document, or a pre-registered client id.

redirectUri.description: Never redirected to before it is matched against the client's registration.

scope.description: Space delimited; absent means "whatever the resource is for".

state.description: Opaque to us, echoed back on the redirect.

codeChallengeMethod.description: Must be `S256`; `plain` is refused rather than downgraded.

resource.description: RFC 8707. Becomes the token's `aud`, which is what keeps it out of the rest of the api.

tenantId.description:
Optional; the user must be an accepted member of that active tenant. Absent means the tenant the approving session
is in, which is what an MCP client gets, since none of them sends this, and Guid Guid.Empty means none,
which the consent page sends when it showed none (See OAuthConsentDto.TenantId). Kept as the raw string so a
malformed one is still malformed when it reaches validation - parsed to null at the boundary, it would read as "no
tenant asked for" and quietly grant the session's tenant instead of `invalid_request`.

OAuthAuthorizeRequestDto.description:
An OAuth 2.1 authorization request, carried unchanged from /oauth/authorize through the consent page and back to
Approve. Property names mirror the wire names because the browser arrives with them in the query string.

clientName.description: Untrusted text the client chose for itself, where one is known.

origin.description: The host it identifies itself by - what an operator should actually read.

activeGrants.description: Live grants to this client. The number that decides whether revoking is safe.

OAuthClientDto.description: One external application as an operator needs to see it.

OAuthClientKind.description: How a client became known. Neither kind is stored, so revoking its grants is all an operator can do.

clientName.description: Untrusted text from a third party. Render as text, never as markup.

clientOrigin.description: The host serving the client's metadata document - the part it cannot forge.

redirectUri.description: Shown because a loopback address means "an app on this machine" and a remote one does not.

isPreRegistered.description: Whether an operator declared this client, rather than it describing itself.

scopes.description: What the token will really carry: requested scopes narrowed to the user's own features.

deniedScopes.description: Scopes the user does not hold. The grant proceeds with what is left, unless nothing is.

tenantId.description:
The tenant the grant will carry, which string? OAuthConsentDto.TenantName names. The consent page sends it back with its
approval, Guid Guid.Empty for none, so the user grants the tenant they saw even if the session has
switched to another one since, in another tab for example.

OAuthConsentDto.description:
What the consent screen shows. Everything here is server-resolved: presenting a client name the browser supplied
would make the request itself the phishing vector.

address.description: The app's address, as the customer typed it: `myapp.com` or `https://myapp.com`.

problemStatusCode.description: The HTTP status a webhook answered with, for ProjectAlertProblem.WebhookRefused.

ProjectAlertRouteDto.description: A way an incident reaches someone, as the Alerts tab edits it (See ProjectAlertRoute on the server).

members.description: Who routes can name; filled by the server, ignored when saving.

key.description: The entry's name in the report, such as `smtp`.

timeoutMs.description: The entry's limit, when the app sets one, to show how close a slow check came.

category.description: The kind of dependency, from the report: Platform, Messaging, Identity, AI, Integrations or the app's own.

title.description: What the app calls the check, such as "Database", in its own words.

about.description: What a pass proves, from the report.

provider.description: What the check talks to, such as "Twilio", from the report.

host.description: The host the check reaches, from the report.

model.description: The model an AI check uses, from the report.

isNotConfigured.description: The check only misses its settings: a setup finding, not an outage.

verifiedAt.description: When the app last really ran a check whose result it reuses; null for one that runs every time.

since.description: Since when the entry has been in this status.

recent.description: The entry in the project's last rounds, oldest first.

ProjectCheckDto.description: One entry of the project's health report, as its Overview shows it.

durationMs.description: Null when the app reused a result it had measured before.

ProjectCheckRoundDto.description: A part of the app in one round.

tone.description: Down when a round found it down, Degraded when one found a part failing, NoData without a round.

uptime.description: The share of the day's rounds the app wasn't down in, as a percentage; null without a round.

ProjectDayDto.description:
A day of a project as its card's bar draws it, from the 15 minute rollups of its report: a round is a minute, so a
round the app didn't answer, or answered Unhealthy, is a minute down, and a Degraded one a minute degraded.

ProjectDayTone.description: How a day of a project went, as History's day bars color it: down beats degraded beats maintenance.

bitProjectId.description: The id in the project's bit.json, once its app or a license named it.

monitorings.description: Its environments, Production first, then by name; each as its card shows it.

ProjectDto.description:
A team's project (bitfabric-internal/specs/monitoring.md, Projects, environments and their people): its card on the
projects page, its row on their Licenses tab, and the head of its page.

ProjectHealth.description: How a project is doing, as its card and its page say it.

periods.description: Each part's stretches in a state other than its first, overlapping the span; open ones have no end.

watchedSince.description: The time before this has no data: the project wasn't watched yet.

parts.description:
The parts History draws a row for, named the way the latest report names them: the latest report's parts, and any
other part that wasn't healthy within the span, but none the latest report says only misses its settings.

reportedFrom.description: The start of its first 15 minutes within the span; null when bit Fabric has no record of it, so it counts from the start.

reportedTo.description: The end of its last 15 minutes within the span; null while the latest report has it.

ProjectHistoryPartDto.description: A part of the app, and the time within the span the app reported it: its days outside that have no data.

ProjectHistoryRequestDto.description: A span of a project's history, which the page draws in the viewer's time zone.

checkTitles.description: What the app calls those parts, in the same order.

agentPrompt.description: Once it's over, a prompt for the customer's AI agent to find the cause in the app's own logs.

ProjectIncidentDto.description: An incident as the project's page shows it, its texts in the reader's language.

until.description: When the trial or the newest license ends or ended; null for none.

oneOf.description: Where the newest license stands; null without one.

licenseId.description: The newest license's id, for the Licenses page; null without one.

ProjectLicenseDto.description: A project's license as the projects' Licenses tab shows it.

ProjectLicenseKind.description: What a project's license is today: what the projects' Licenses tab and the AI tools say of it.

checkedAt.description: When the newest report was read; null before the first one.

homePageMs.description: How long the app's own page took in that round.

parts.description: The parts of the app, by the report's categories, as its last report lists them.

ProjectMapDto.description:
A project's application map (bitfabric-internal/specs/monitoring.md, Application map): everything its last health report
says the app talks to, each part with how it's doing now and over the last 24 hours.

key.description: The entry's name in the report, such as `smtp`.

title.description: What the app calls it, such as "Database", in its own words.

category.description: The kind of dependency, from the report: Platform, Messaging, Identity, AI, Integrations or the app's own.

about.description: What a pass proves, from the report.

provider.description:
What lies behind the part, such as "Twilio" behind "SMS": the outside service the app's report says the check talks
to. Null when the report names none; bit Fabric never guesses it.

host.description: The host the check reaches, from the report.

model.description: The model an AI check uses, from the report.

isNotConfigured.description: Its settings are missing: a setup finding, not an outage.

since.description: Since when it has been in this status.

checkedAt.description: When the app last really ran it: the round's time, or earlier for a result the app reuses.

lastMs.description: How long its last real run took.

typicalMs.description: The average of its timed runs over the last 24 hours.

slowestMs.description: Its slowest run over the last 24 hours.

rounds.description: The rounds that looked at it over the last 24 hours.

problemRounds.description: The rounds of the last 24 hours it failed or was degraded in.

ongoingIncidentId.description: The ongoing incident about it, if there is one.

ProjectMapPartDto.description: One thing the app depends on, such as its database or its email service, as its report names it.

isMember.description: A member of the project; otherwise someone of the team who can be added.

addedOn.description: When they became a member; null for one who isn't.

alertRouteCount.description: The project's environments whose alerts reach them.

ProjectMemberDto.description: Someone of the team, and whether they work on the project.

colo.description: The data center the reading ran in, such as `IAD`: a location is a hint, which Cloudflare follows as best it can.

responseMs.description: Null when the app didn't answer from there.

ProjectNetworkReadingDto.description: A reading of the bitplatform Network: how long the home page took from one location, and where it really ran.

stepMinutes.description: How many minutes each point covers, which may be wider than asked.

starts.description: The deployments and restarts in the span.

ProjectPerformanceDto.description: How long each part of a project took over a span of time, a point per bar (bitfabric-internal/specs/monitoring.md, Performance).

failed.description: The rounds it was Unhealthy in, or didn't answer.

averageMs.description: The average time of the rounds that timed it; null when none answered.

stepMinutes.description: 1 for every round, 15, 60, 360 or 1440 from the rollups.

ProjectPerformanceRequestDto.description:
What the Performance tab asks for: a span of a project's history and how many minutes a bar may cover. The server may
make the bars wider, so no row gets more than it can draw.

ProjectPerformanceSeriesDto.description: One part from one region: a report entry's key, `$home` for the home page or `$report` for the report.

ProjectScanDevice.description: What a browser scan loaded a page as: Lighthouse's mobile (a mid-range phone on a slow 4G network) or desktop.

applicationVersion.description: The build the deployment brought, for a scan after a deployment.

requestedAt.description: When it was asked for; a deployment's scans are asked for a couple of minutes after it.

startedAt.description: Null while it waits for its turn.

finishedAt.description: Null while it waits or runs.

score.description: Security's points, and the 0 to 100 of SEO, Performance and Accessibility (the lowest of the pages and devices measured).

grade.description: Security's grade, A+ to F, from int? ProjectScanDto.Score.

expiresAt.description: Domain and certificate: when the first of the app's certificates and domain registrations ends.

pages.description: Performance and Accessibility: each page and device measured, the home page on a phone first.

findings.description: Most urgent first; filled for the latest runs and for a run asked for by itself.

ProjectScanDto.description: One run of one kind of scan on a project.

key.description: One of ScanFindings' keys, such as `CspMissing`.

parameters.description: The values its texts are formatted with, in order, such as a host name and a number of days.

where.description: Where bit Fabric saw it: page paths, host names or addresses.

isReportedWrong.description: Someone of the team marked it "this is wrong".

ProjectScanFindingDto.description:
What a scan found, as a stable key and its parameters rather than text, so each viewer reads it in their own language
(See ScanFindings for the texts, and ScanPrompts for the prompt for the customer's AI agent).

oneOf.description: One kind's runs, or every kind's when null.

ProjectScanKind.description:
The scans bit Fabric runs on a project (bitfabric-internal/specs/scanners.md). The numbers are stored, so a kind keeps
its number when others are added.

path.description: The page's path, as it answered after its redirects, such as /en-US/.

score.description: 0 to 100: this kind's Lighthouse score of the page.

ProjectScanPageDto.description:
One page a browser scan loaded, on one device, with its score and, for Performance, the Core Web Vitals Lighthouse
measured (bitfabric-internal/specs/scanners.md, Decisions). Lab numbers: TBT stands in for INP, which needs a real user's interaction.

address.description: The project's address, which the prompts for the customer's AI agent name.

latest.description: The newest finished run of each kind, with its findings, in the order the tab shows them.

pending.description: The runs waiting for their turn or running, a kind at most once.

canRunAgainAt.description: When "Run scans now" may be pressed again; null when it may now.

ProjectScansDto.description: A project's Scans tab: the latest run of each kind with what it found, and when bit Fabric scans.

scanAfterDeployments.description: Off until the owner allows it: bit Fabric sees each deployment in the health check.

weeklyEmail.description:
The project is in the weekly scans email its team's members get (bitfabric-internal/specs/scanners.md, Decisions):
on until someone turns it off.

ProjectScanSettingsDto.description: When bit Fabric scans a project (bitfabric-internal/specs/scanners.md, Decisions, 2026-11-13).

scanId.description: The newest finished run of this kind; null when none has.

isRunning.description: It waits for its turn or runs.

finishedAt.description: When the newest finished run of this kind finished; null when none has.

oneOf.description: The most urgent finding, which the card shows as its tooltip.

ProjectScanSummaryDto.description: A project's newest scan of one kind, as its card on the projects page shows it.

ProjectScanTrigger.description: Why a scan ran (after every deployment, on a schedule and by hand).

projectId.description: The project it is an environment of, whose name string? ProjectSettingsDto.Name is.

environment.description: This environment's name: Production, Test, Staging or one the team gives.

timeZoneId.description: The IANA time zone an SLA month follows.

approvedBy.description: Who approved bit Fabric in the app; read only.

reads.description: The one address bit Fabric reads with that approval; read only.

ProjectSlaCreditDto.description: A tier of the owner's contract with their customers: a month below double ProjectSlaCreditDto.BelowPercent gives double ProjectSlaCreditDto.CreditPercent back.

minutes.description: The minutes of it the count left out: those of the month that bit Fabric watched and that have passed.

ProjectSlaMaintenanceDto.description: A maintenance window's occurrence in the month, left out of the count.

availability.description: The app's availability that month; null when it wasn't watched.

timeZoneId.description: The IANA time zone the month runs in (bitfabric-internal/specs/monitoring.md, Times follow the viewer's time zone).

from.description: Midnight of the month's first day in the project's time zone, as an instant.

to.description: Midnight of the next month's first day in the project's time zone, as an instant.

isCurrent.description: The month is still running, so its figures are so far.

settings.description: The target, weights and credits the figures were counted with.

app.description: The app as a whole, from its incidents: the month's figure.

parts.description: Each part of the app, from its own periods and the app's outages.

budgetMinutes.description: The weighted minutes of outage the target allows in the month.

leftMinutes.description: What is left of double ProjectSlaReportDto.BudgetMinutes after the app's weighted minutes; never below zero.

oneOf.description: The credit tier the month falls into, if any.

months.description: The last 12 months, oldest first, this one last.

maintenanceMinutes.description: Maintenance left out of the count, the incidents that began in it included.

noDataMinutes.description: Time bit Fabric couldn't read the app's report, such as while it needed reconnecting.

notWatchedMinutes.description: Time of the month before bit Fabric watched the app.

ProjectSlaReportDto.description: A month's SLA report (bitfabric-internal/specs/monitoring.md, SLA reports), on the SLA tab and in its CSV and PDF.

year.description: The month's year in the project's time zone; null with int? ProjectSlaRequestDto.Month for this month.

key.description: The part's report key; null for the app as a whole.

title.description: What the app calls the part, or the project's name.

availability.description: A percentage; null when no minute of the month counted.

countedMinutes.description: The minutes the formula counts: watched, read, and outside maintenance.

weightedMinutes.description: Down, plus partial and degraded each times its weight: what the error budget is spent on.

ProjectSlaRowDto.description: A month of the app, or of one of its parts, in minutes, and the availability they make with the report's weights.

targetPercent.description: The availability promised a month, such as 99.9.

partialWeight.description: How much of a minute of partial outage counts as down, 0 to 1.

degradedWeight.description: How much of a minute a part is slow but works counts as down, 0 to 1.

ProjectSlaSettingsDto.description:
What the owner promises and how the SLA counts (bitfabric-internal/specs/monitoring.md, SLA reports): the target, the
weights of a partial outage and of a slow part, and the credit tiers of their contract. Defaults are 99.9%, 30% and
0%, with no credit tiers until the owner enters theirs.

ProjectTeamMemberDto.description: A member of the project's team, who an alert can reach.

stretches.description: Its stretches down or degraded over the last 90 days, from its incidents.

isFallback.description: Not written in the visitor's language: shown in the page's main one.

appAddress.description: The app's own address, which the page links back to.

iconId.description: The app's own icon, an attachment of its own (See MonitoringDto.IconId); null for none, and the page shows a monogram.

state.description: Operational, Degraded, Down, or NoData when bit Fabric can't read the app right now.

culture.description: The culture the texts are in.

languages.description: The languages the owner writes in, the main one first.

medianResponseMs.description: The home page's median time over the last 24 hours, past any cache: the server's own.

medianVisitorMs.description: The median time a visitor waited for it, through the cache in front of the app; null when no cache answered.

pushPublicKey.description: The Web Push public key a visitor's browser subscribes with; null where push isn't set up.

maintenance.description: Maintenance windows going on or coming in the next 30 days.

history.description: The incidents and announcements of the last 90 days that are over, newest first.

PublicStatusDto.description: A status page as a visitor sees it, in their language; no report key or description leaves bit Fabric.

oneOf.description: A WebAuthn assertion offered in place of string? RefreshTokenRequestDto.ElevatedAccessToken (See IdentityController.ElevateByWebAuthn).

requestedTenantId.description:
The id of the tenant the user is trying to switch into.
If it has a value and the user has such an active tenant, then that id will be stored as the string AppClaimTypes.TENANT_ID claim,
otherwise the user gets kicked out. When it's null, the tenant id of the passed refresh token remains unchanged.

note.description: What they think is wrong about it, if they say.

ReportScanFindingRequestDto.description: A team member says a finding is wrong (bitfabric-internal/specs/scanners.md, A wrong finding can be reported).

returnUrl.description: URL for redirection after user confirmation, used when sending a confirmation email to an unconfirmed user.

RevokeOAuthClientRequestDto.description: A body rather than a route segment, because a client id can be a url hundreds of characters long.

ScanFindingSeverity.description: How soon a finding wants fixing; the report ranks urgent first.

pageUrl.description: The page to be opened when the notification is clicked.

returnUrl.description: URL for redirection after user confirmation, used when sending a confirmation email to an unconfirmed user.

locations.description: Codes of NetworkLocations; none leaves only bit Fabric's own server in Germany.

SetProjectLocationsRequestDto.description: The bitplatform Network's locations a project is checked from, replacing the ones it had.

twoFactorCode.description: Two factor code generated by authenticator app

returnUrl.description: URL for redirection after user confirmation, used when sending a confirmation email to an unconfirmed user.
URL for redirection after user confirmation, used when sending a confirmation email to an unconfirmed user.

projectId.description:
The project the environment joins, from its page's "Add an environment"; null for a new project named
string? StartConnectRequestDto.Name. Either way, a project of the team with the id the app reports takes it instead.

environment.description: Production, Test, Staging or a name the team gives; Production when empty.

localHttpPort.description: The native app's local server, which the approval's answer goes back to (See ILocalHttpServer); null on the web.

authorizeUrl.description: The customer app's sign-in and approval page, which opens beside the add page.

chatMessagesHistory.description: The conversation so far, trusted and trimmed as the text chat's is (See `AppChatbot.BelievableHistory`).

maxDuration.description: The server hangs up once the call reaches this.

StatusComponentDto.description: A part of the app as its users know it, its name and description in each language the owner writes.

slug.description: The page is at `/status/{slug}`: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.

languages.description: The languages the owner writes updates in, the main one first.

publicUrl.description: Where the page is: bit Fabric's address for it, or the customer's own once it's active. Read only.

customHostname.description: Such as `status.myapp.com`. Read only: connected through `ConnectCustomHostname`.

customHostnameState.description: Cloudflare's state of that host name, such as "pending" or "active". Read only.

cnameTarget.description: What the customer's CNAME record points at. Read only; null while custom host names aren't set up.

followerCount.description: How many browsers and devices follow the page. Read only.

checks.description: The report entries a component can be made of, with what the app calls them. Read only.

StatusPageSettingsDto.description: A project's status page as its owner edits it (bitfabric-internal/specs/monitoring.md, Status page).

incidentId.description: An update to this incident; null for a new one.

impact.description: Degraded or Down for an incident.

title.description: The title in each language, by culture name; a new one needs at least the page's main language.

text.description: What the team says, in each language.

notifiesFollowers.description: Whether the page's followers get a push about it, in their language.

StatusPostRequestDto.description: An incident, an update to one, or an announcement the team posts (bitfabric-internal/specs/monitoring.md, Posting an update).

signature.description: What the server signed string SynthesizeSpeechRequestDto.Text with when it wrote it (string? AiChatMessage.Signature).

SynthesizeSpeechRequestDto.description: The text to read out loud. See `ChatbotController.SynthesizeSpeech`.

currentUserMembershipStatus.description:
The current user's membership state for this tenant: TenantMembershipStatus.Member when she has
accepted it, TenantMembershipStatus.Invited when she has been invited but hasn't accepted yet (See
`TenantMembership.AcceptedOn`), and TenantMembershipStatus.None when she has no membership row
at all - which only happens for a global admin, who is listed every active tenant whether or not she belongs to it.
Only populated by `UserController.GetTenants`.

text.description:
Empty rather than null when the recording carried no speech - a user who taps the microphone and says nothing
gets an empty box, not an error.

TranscribeSpeechResponseDto.description: What the server heard in a recording the AI chat panel sent it. See `ChatbotController.TranscribeSpeech`.

project.description: The project's id, which `bit new` writes into bit.json as `projectId`.

commit.description: The full sha of the project's first git commit.

ci.description:
The CI bit CLI asks from, by the name it gives it (`github-actions`, `other`, ...); null outside CI. bit
Fabric keeps it only to count such trials apart: the trial is the same, as long, and allows the same.

TrialLicenseRequestDto.description: What `bit new` sends for a new project's trial, right after the project's first commit.

appVersion.description: The version of that application that the user is using in this session.

cultureName.description: The culture selected by the user in this session.

notificationStatus.description: The device's own choice (See NotificationPreferenceService), so a new sign-in on it follows what it was set to.

authenticationMethod.description:
How this session signed in - Password, Email, Sms, Push, External (social) or WebAuthn. Easier to recognise a
session by than its IP. See `UserSession.AuthenticationMethod`.

signalRConnectionId.description: The most recently connected tab or app of this session, not all of them. See `UserSession.SignalRConnectionId`.

cultureName.description: The culture selected by the user for this session.

appVersionCode.description:
The version of the application used for this session, as a sortable number so an OData filter or sort over it
means what it says - see AppVersionCodes.

oAuthClientId.description:
Set when this session belongs to an external app authorized over OAuth. Surfaced in the sessions list because a
grant to somebody else's software is what a user most needs to recognise before revoking it.

oAuthClientName.description: The application's own name, where it gave one. Untrusted text: render as text, never as markup.

oAuthScope.description: Space delimited, as granted - what this application may actually do, rather than merely that it can.

UserSessionNotificationStatus.description:
Whether a session receives notifications - push and SignalR's in-app SHOW_MESSAGE alike. The device reports it on
every UpdateSession from the switch in AppMenu, so a session only follows that device's own choice.

userIds.description:
The user ids whose credential descriptors should be offered to the authenticator. The real flow sends
the ids the client already holds in local storage, which is a handful - the cap is here because the
endpoint is anonymous and the list was otherwise unbounded.

Bearer.description: Get your JWT token by signing in through the Identity/SignIn endpoint.
